name: Pharmaceutical Nanotechnology Research Laboratory

institute: National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER), Hyderabad
intro: PNRL works at the interface of advanced material science, nanotechnology and biopharmaceutics — engineering translational nanomedicines that overcome biological barriers and the solubility, permeability and toxicity limits of challenging therapeutics.
about: The Pharmaceutical Nanotechnology Research Laboratory (PNRL) at NIPER Hyderabad, directed by Dr. Neelesh Kumar Mehra, operates at the interface of advanced material science, nanotechnology, and biopharmaceutics. The laboratory focuses on engineering translational, smart nanomedicines to overcome biological barriers and solve critical solubility, permeability, and toxicity limitations of challenging therapeutics.

By integrating molecular biopharmaceutics, mechanistic pharmacokinetic/PBPK modeling, and targeted delivery strategies, the group develops innovative therapeutic platforms for oncology, resistant infections, ocular disorders, and chronic inflammatory diseases. PNRL bridges academic discoveries with bench-to-bedside translational drug delivery.
history: Established within the Department of Pharmaceutics at NIPER Hyderabad under Dr. Neelesh Kumar Mehra, the laboratory emerged as a specialized center for targeted formulation science and molecular drug delivery. Over the years, the lab has trained numerous M.S. (Pharm.) and Ph.D. scholars, publishing extensively in premier international drug delivery journals and collaborating with national laboratories, biomedical institutes, and pharmaceutical R&D facilities.

mission.title: Engineer
mission.text: Engineer biocompatible, smart nanoplatforms for targeted therapeutic delivery with minimal systemic toxicity.

mission.title: Train
mission.text: Foster rigorous interdisciplinary training for postgraduate and doctoral scholars in advanced drug delivery science, regulatory expectations, and pre-clinical formulation development.

mission.title: Translate
mission.text: Bridge bench research and translational clinical technologies through industry-academia linkages and inter-institutional collaborations.

objectives: Design and surface-engineer polymeric, lipid, and hybrid nano-architectures for targeted chemotherapy and immunotherapy.
Solve poor aqueous solubility and bioavailability of BCS Class II/IV compounds via co-amorphous systems, nanocrystals, and solid lipid dispersions.
Investigate cellular uptake, pharmacokinetic behavior, tissue distribution, and PBPK modeling of novel formulation systems.
Develop non-invasive delivery modalities (topical, mucosal, ocular, and oral) for complex synthetic and biological molecules.

research.title: Functionalized carbon nanotubes
research.text: Surface-functionalized nanotubes as high-payload carriers for site-specific delivery.

research.title: Surface-tailored dendrimers
research.text: Branched, surface-engineered macromolecules and dendrimer conjugates for targeted therapy.

research.title: Polymeric / lipid hybrid nanoparticles
research.text: PLGA, lipid and lipid–polymer hybrid nano-architectures for targeted chemo- and immunotherapy.

research.title: Transferosomes & vesicles
research.text: Deformable vesicles and liposomes for topical, mucosal and ocular delivery.

research.title: Solid dispersions & nanocrystals
research.text: Crystalline and co-amorphous systems that lift the solubility and bioavailability of BCS Class II/IV drugs.

research.title: PK & PBPK modeling
research.text: Mechanistic pharmacokinetics, tissue distribution and PBPK modeling of novel formulations.
